title: Integrated transcriptomic, molecular docking, and mendelian randomization analysis reveal a microbial-propionate-JUN pathway in renal ischemia-reperfusion injury.
authors: Li, Jun; Huang, Ruizhen; Wang, Xing; Zhang, Yunfeng; Xu, Zuhuan; Zhang, Penglin; Hu, Honglin
one_liner_zh: 该研究整合转录组、孟德尔随机化和分子对接分析微生物-丙酸-JUN通路在肾缺血再灌注损伤中的作用，虽涉及蛋白-小分子对接，但核心非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或MD方法，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is a major cause of acute kidney injury and is characterized by oxidative stress, immune cell infiltration, and inflammatory signaling activation. Although gut microbiota and their metabolites, especially short-chain fatty acids, are involved in systemic immune regulation, their role in renal IRI remains unclear. Here, we integrated transcriptomic analysis, gut-derived metabolite target prediction, molecular docking, and Mendelian randomization (MR) to explore potential microbiota-metabolite-host regulatory mechanisms in renal IRI. We identified 32 target genes of gut-derived metabolites using the gutMGene, Similarity Ensemble Approach, and SwissTargetPrediction databases. In two renal IRI datasets (GSE126805 and GSE90861), 263 and 641 differentially expressed genes were identified, respectively, and hub genes were mainly enriched in the TNF and IL-17 signaling pathways. Among them, JUN was identified as a key hub linking gut microbiota-associated metabolites to renal inflammatory signaling. MR analysis showed that Akkermansia muciniphila was positively associated with kidney injury susceptibility [p = 0.026, odds ratio (OR) = 1.219], whereas Ruminococcus bromii was negatively associated with kidney injury susceptibility (p = 0.011, OR = 0.740). Because propionate, rather than butyrate, was the shared metabolite associated with both taxa, subsequent analyses focused on the propionate-JUN interaction. Molecular docking and dynamics supported strong binding between propionate and JUN. Overall, these findings suggest a potential gut-kidney regulatory axis involving A. muciniphila/R. bromii-propionate-JUN-TNF/IL-17 signaling in renal IRI, providing new insight into microbiota-associated mechanisms of renal inflammatory injury.
abstract_zh: 肾缺血再灌注损伤（IRI）是急性肾损伤的主要原因，其特征为氧化应激、免疫细胞浸润和炎症信号激活。尽管肠道微生物群及其代谢产物，尤其是短链脂肪酸，参与全身免疫调节，但其在肾IRI中的作用仍不清楚。在此，我们整合了转录组分析、肠道来源代谢物靶点预测、分子对接和孟德尔随机化（MR），以探索肾IRI中潜在的微生物-代谢物-宿主调控机制。我们利用gutMGene、Similarity Ensemble Approach和SwissTargetPrediction数据库鉴定了肠道来源代谢物的32个靶基因。在两个肾IRI数据集（GSE126805和GSE90861）中，分别鉴定出263和641个差异表达基因，枢纽基因主要富集于TNF和IL-17信号通路。其中，JUN被确定为连接肠道微生物相关代谢物与肾炎症信号的关键枢纽。MR分析显示，Akkermansia muciniphila与肾损伤易感性呈正相关[p = 0.026，比值比（OR）= 1.219]，而Ruminococcus bromii与肾损伤易感性呈负相关（p = 0.011，OR = 0.740）。由于丙酸盐（而非丁酸盐）是与这两种菌群相关的共有代谢物，后续分析聚焦于丙酸盐-JUN相互作用。分子对接和动力学支持丙酸盐与JUN之间的强结合。总体而言，这些发现提示肾IRI中存在一个涉及A. muciniphila/R. bromii-丙酸盐-JUN-TNF/IL-17信号的潜在肠-肾调控轴，为肾炎症损伤的微生物相关机制提供了新见解。
